content.text:
**$6,748.13 of Luka's $7,000 conversion is taxable income for 2025. Only $251.87 comes out tax-free.** The other $6,748.13 of his after-tax money stays in his traditional IRAs and carries forward to 2026 as basis.

**Why:** His rollover IRA (SYN-12040002) was still open at year-end. For the tax calculation, all of a person's traditional IRAs count as one pot. So the conversion can't come only from the $7,000 he put in after tax. It comes proportionally from after-tax and pre-tax money.

**Form 8606 calculation**
| Line | | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2025 nondeductible contribution (SYN-12040003, 2025-02-10) | $7,000.00 |
| 2 | Basis from earlier years (tax profile, as of 2024-12-31) | $0.00 |
| 6 | Traditional IRAs at 2025-12-31 (rollover IRA $42,871.51 Larkspur Core Bond Fund + $142,362.18 Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund + $2,311.23 cash; SYN-12040003 $0) | $187,544.92 |
| 8 | Converted to Roth 2025-02-13 | $7,000.00 |
| 9 | Line 6 + line 8 | $194,544.92 |
| 10 | Line 5 ÷ line 9 | 0.035981 |
| 11 | Tax-free part of the conversion | $251.87 |
| 14 | Basis carried to 2026 | $6,748.13 |
| 18 | Taxable part of the conversion | $6,748.13 |

If line 10 is rounded to three places (0.036), the taxable amount and the basis become $6,748.00.

- **The 1099-R is incomplete.** It shows $7,000 with "taxable amount not determined" checked. Unless the return includes Form 8606, the full $7,000 could be taxed and the basis lost.
- **Deadline:** today, 15 April 2026, is the filing deadline. The files don't say who prepares the return or whether it has been filed.
- **Why there's no deductibility issue:** the W-2s don't show whether either spouse is in a workplace plan. That doesn't affect the answer, because the contribution was planned as nondeductible.
- **The cause:** the December 2024 plan kept the rollover IRA "as it is". That is why part of the conversion is taxable.

**What I wrote to the CRM (HH-1204, dated 2026-04-15)**
- **Note SB-1204-01:** the finding and every figure above. I wrote the decisions as the firm's position: pass the figures to the tax preparer, and hold off on a 2026 conversion until the rollover IRA is dealt with. The files don't record a decision by the clients, so edit this if the meeting settles something different.
- **Activity SB-1204-02:** confirm who prepares the return and whether it's filed or extended, and send them the Form 8606 figures and the 1099-R. If it was filed without Form 8606, ask the preparer about amending.
- **Activity SB-1204-03:** once the filed Form 8606 is confirmed, update Luka's IRA basis in the portfolio system to $6,748.13 as of 2025-12-31 (it still shows $0.00 as of 2024-12-31). I can't write to the portfolio system, so this is a task.
- **Activity SB-1204-04:** before any 2026 conversion, Luka asks whether his employer's plan accepts incoming IRA rollovers. Moving the rollover IRA ($202,112.10 at 2026-03-31) into it by 31 Dec 2026 would keep 2026 from repeating this result. The files don't confirm he has a plan there.
